newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool indicator falls 7c to 593c/kg.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool indicator falls 7c to 593c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market continued to decline at auctions in Sydney and Melbourne on Tuesday and the eastern market indicator fell 7.0 cents to 593 cents a kg clean Wool International (WI) said.
In merinos, the 19/21/23 micron indicators were 1.0 percent cheaper, 20/22/26m up to 1.5 percent cheaper, 24m 0.5 percent cheaper and 25m 2.0 percent cheaper, WI said.
In merino skirtings, 19m was slightly dearer and 20/21/22m 1.5 percent cheaper.
In crossbreds, 27m was 1.0 percent cheaper, 28/29m up to 0.5 percent cheaper and 30/31m up to 1.0 percent dearer.
In cardings, lambs were 1.5 percent dearer, locks up to 1.0 percent cheaper and crutchings up to 1.0 percent dearer.
Japanese interests provided principal competition with good support from Western Europe, WI said.
Of the 20,950 bales offered in Sydney and Melbourne, 18.1 percent were passed in.
Sales continue on Thursday in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with about 43,000 bales on offer.
